t: LIABILITY FOR MALICIOUS SOLICITATION DURING DISASTER

l: In this chapter, "malicious solicitation during a disaster" means conduct that constitutes an offense under Section 32.61, Penal Code.

A person who engages in malicious solicitation during a disaster is liable to the donee on whose behalf the payment was collected, the donee's estate, the donor from whom the payment was solicited, or the donor's estate.
(a) A court shall award a donee or donee's estate who prevails in an action brought under this chapter:
(1) 300 percent of the amount of donations the defendant collected on behalf of the donee; and
(b) A court shall award a donor or a donor's estate who prevails in an action brought under this chapter:
(1) 300 percent of the amount of donations the defendant collected from the donor; and

(c) Nothing in this section prevents a donee, donee's estate, donor, or donor's estate from pursuing a claim for exemplary damages under Chapter 41 for the defendant's malicious solicitation during a disaster.
